objective: Convert the audited ONE TALIBON React/Vite functional prototype into an authoritative React/Vite + Laravel JSON API + PostgreSQL system while preserving valuable UX and replacing browser-local authority, simulated security, fake file handling, and documentation-only production claims.

decisions.authentication: ONE TALIBON local username/password with real TOTP MFA
decisions.frontend: Keep existing React/Vite frontend and rewire it to a Laravel JSON API
decisions.session: Same-origin Laravel Sanctum cookie session with CSRF protection; no LocalStorage identity/session authority
decisions.rosterAuthority: All current office/employee/person/contact seed data is DEMO DATA until an LGU-authoritative roster is supplied, even if any value was sourced from the public web
decisions.files: Laravel private filesystem storage plus PostgreSQL metadata and authorization-gated download endpoints

workPackage.goal: Build the authoritative full-stack ONE TALIBON common core from the existing audited prototype.

auditCriticalFindings: No real authentication; persona switching is identity takeover.
Authorization is client-side and inconsistent; permissions[] is effectively unused.
Audit trail is mutable LocalStorage, not immutable.
MFA is a boolean/method flag, not cryptographic MFA.
Unauthorized data already exists in the browser store before filtering.
PostgreSQL and Laravel are documentation targets only, not runtime.
Documents are metadata simulations; no file bytes, SHA-256, secure download, MIME validation, or storage.
Workflow configuration does not govern actual task/work-request execution.
No queue, scheduler, email/SMS delivery, durable multi-user state, or concurrency guarantees.
Backup/restore was not executed and must not be reported PASS.
removeOrRebuild: hard-coded or invented official KPIs/policy claims
any official-roster wording for demo data
